learning_outcomes.text: Correctly use chemical nomenclature and language.
Understand the basic principles of matter constitution, bonding, and structure.
Know the relationship between structure and physical and chemical properties of organic and inorganic compounds.
Solve problems related to chemical reactivity, the interaction of chemical products with the environment, and the stability of different types of materials.
Be able to perform calculations based on stoichiometry, interpret relevant data and results.
Know, theoretically and practically, the basic operations of a chemical laboratory.
Know and apply the chemical fundamentals of Engineering.
Be able to transmit information, ideas, and conclusions.

syllabus_topics: Organic acid-base, oxidation, condensation and polymerization reactions
Thermochemistry, heat of reaction and Hess's Law (Practical)
Analysis of the acidity of a commercial product (Practical)
Reducing power of metals. Electrochemical scale. Cells (Practical)

assessment_methods.method: Experimental work: Laboratory work and reports

assessment_rules: To pass the course, a minimum grade of 5 out of 10 must be obtained in the Long Answer Test. A minimum grade of 5 out of 10 is also required in the weighted average of the "Experimental Work: Laboratory work and reports" and "Experimental Work: Exam" components. If the course is not passed, the numerical grade will be the weighted average if it is less than 5, or 4.9 if the weighted average results in a value greater than 5.0.
